title: Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
abstract-summary: Information-theoretic argument (Data Processing Inequality) showing single agents match or beat multi-agent under equal token budgets across multiple models.
notes: SA consistently matches or exceeds MA when thinking-token budget is held constant. Concludes that reported MA advantages stem from unaccounted computation rather than architectural benefits.

title: Rethinking the Value of Multi-Agent Workflow: A Strong Single Agent Baseline
abstract-summary: Shows a single agent via multi-turn conversation can match homogeneous multi-agent workflows across 7 benchmarks with efficiency gains from KV cache reuse.
benchmark: coding; math; QA; domain-specific reasoning; planning; tool-use
notes: Proposes OneFlow algorithm. Single agent matches homogeneous MA workflows. Highlights that most MA frameworks are homogeneous (same base LLM) so a single agent can replicate them.

title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
abstract-summary: Systematic evaluation of 5 MAD methods across 9 benchmarks using 4 foundation models. MAD fails to reliably outperform CoT and self-consistency.
notes: MAD methods fail to reliably outperform simple single-agent baselines (CoT and Self-Consistency) even when consuming additional inference-time computation. Critical shortcomings in evaluation practices identified.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
abstract-summary: Introduces MAST taxonomy with 14 failure modes across 1600+ annotated traces from 7 MAS frameworks. Performance gains across popular benchmarks remain minimal.
notes: 14 unique failure modes in 3 categories: system design issues; inter-agent misalignment; task verification. High inter-annotator agreement (kappa=0.88). Accepted NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks track.

title: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
abstract-summary: Models frequently shift from correct to incorrect answers during debate. Weak agents can detrimentally affect strong agents. Longer debates can degrade performance.
notes: Introducing a weak LLM into debate with a strong LLM produces results worse than no debate. Performance can degrade the longer debate continues. Sycophancy and social conformity identified as contributing factors.

title: Peacemaker or Troublemaker: How Sycophancy Shapes Multi-Agent Debate
abstract-summary: First operational framework defining sycophancy in MAD. Higher debater sycophancy strongly associated with failures to reach correct conclusions during disagreements.
notes: Sycophantic behavior undermines performance by encouraging premature consensus and reducing decision quality. Proposes spectrum from troublemaker (independent reasoning) to peacemaker (agreement-seeking).

title: Can LLM Agents Really Debate? A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent Debate in Logical Reasoning
abstract-summary: Controlled study using Knight-Knave-Spy puzzles. Intrinsic reasoning strength and group diversity are dominant drivers; structural debate parameters (order; confidence visibility) offer limited gains.
notes: Debate structure provides minimal improvement. The gains come from agent diversity and intrinsic capability rather than the debate mechanism itself.

title: Stay Focused: Problem Drift in Multi-Agent Debate
authors: Becker; Kaesberg; Stephan; Wahle; Ruas; Gipp
abstract-summary: Quantifies problem drift across 10 tasks. Generative tasks drift 76-89% of the time. Root causes: lack of progress (35%); low-quality feedback (26%); lack of clarity (25%).
notes: Problem drift causes performance decay over debate rounds. Proposes DRIFTJudge for detection and DRIFTPolicy mitigates 31% of drift cases. 170 debates analyzed by 8 human experts.

title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
abstract-summary: Disentangles MAD into voting and debate components. Majority voting alone accounts for most performance gains attributed to MAD. Debate induces a martingale over belief trajectories.
notes: Proves debate alone does not improve expected correctness (martingale property). Most performance gains from MAD are actually from ensembling/majority voting not the debate mechanism.

title: Understanding Agent Scaling in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Diversity
abstract-summary: Scaling homogeneous agents shows strong diminishing returns. Performance bounded by intrinsic task uncertainty not agent count. Diversity is key not quantity.
notes: Homogeneous agent scaling: marginal gain collapses toward zero. Output correlation creates redundancy. Heterogeneity (different models; prompts; tools) sustains improvement where homogeneous scaling fails.

title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
abstract-summary: 260 configurations across 6 benchmarks; 5 architectures; 3 LLM families. Identifies capability-saturation effect. Coordination yields diminishing returns once SA baselines exceed certain performance.
notes: Derives quantitative scaling law. Tool-heavy tasks incur multi-agent overhead. Architectures without centralized verification propagate errors more. Challenges assumption that increasing agent count monotonically improves performance.

title: HiddenBench: Assessing Collective Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs via Hidden Profile Tasks
abstract-summary: Multi-agent LLMs achieve only 30.1% accuracy under distributed information vs 80.7% for single agents with complete information.
notes: Agents cannot recognize latent information asymmetry. Premature convergence on shared evidence. Failures persist across prompting strategies and worsen as groups scale.

title: From Spark to Fire: Modeling and Mitigating Error Cascades in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
authors: Xie; Zhu; Zhang; Zhu; Ye; Qi; Chen; Zhou
abstract-summary: Error propagation dynamics model for LLM-MAS. Identifies three vulnerability classes: cascade amplification; topological sensitivity; consensus inertia.
notes: Minor inaccuracies solidify into system-level false consensus through iteration. Errors propagate and amplify through message dependencies. Proposes genealogy-graph governance raising defense from 0.32 to 0.89.

title: Debate Only When Necessary: Adaptive Multiagent Collaboration for Efficient LLM Reasoning
abstract-summary: Shows unnecessary debate increases risk of erroneous responses. Proposes DOWN framework that selectively activates debate based on confidence.
notes: Engaging in unnecessary debates increases error risk. DOWN improves efficiency by 6x while matching or outperforming existing MAD methods. Validates that debate is often counterproductive.

title: When Identity Skews Debate: Anonymization for Bias-Reduced Multi-Agent Reasoning
abstract-summary: Identity-driven sycophancy and self-bias undermine MAD reliability. Formalizes debate dynamics as identity-weighted Bayesian update. Proposes anonymization as mitigation.
notes: Agents prone to identity-driven sycophancy (uncritically adopting peer views) and self-bias (stubbornly adhering to own output). Anonymization removes identity markers to force equal weighting.

title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
abstract-summary: Benchmarks range of MAD strategies. MAD does not reliably outperform self-consistency and ensembling. MAD is more sensitive to hyperparameters and harder to optimize.
notes: MAD systems do not reliably outperform other prompting strategies. MAD is more sensitive to hyperparameter settings and difficult to optimize compared to simpler baselines.

title: Conformity in Large Language Models
abstract-summary: All tested LLMs exhibit conformity toward majority regardless of correctness. Models more likely to conform when uncertain. Instruction-tuned models less susceptible.
notes: First to show LLMs conform more when uncertain. In multi-agent debate this creates echo chambers where agents converge on incorrect answers with high apparent confidence.

title: Demystifying Multi-Agent Debate: The Role of Confidence and Diversity
authors: Zhu; Zhang; Chi; Stafford; Collier; Vlachos
abstract-summary: Vanilla MAD often underperforms simple majority vote despite higher computational cost. Identifies two missing mechanisms: diversity of viewpoints and calibrated confidence.
notes: Vanilla MAD underperforms majority vote. Proposes diversity-aware initialization and confidence-modulated debate to fix. Demonstrates current MAD wastes compute.

title: Revisiting Multi-Agent Debate as Test-Time Scaling: A Systematic Study of Conditional Effectiveness
abstract-summary: MAD offers only limited advantages over self-agent scaling for solution-finding tasks even with diverse agents. Effectiveness increases slightly with difficulty.
notes: For solution-finding tasks MAD provides limited advantage over single-agent test-time scaling. Only safety/judging tasks show consistent MAD benefit with diverse agents.

title: AgentAsk: Multi-Agent Systems Need to Ask
abstract-summary: Identifies four dominant error types at inter-agent handoffs: Data Gap; Signal Corruption; Referential Drift; Capability Gap. MA systems fail to outperform strong SA baselines due to error propagation.
notes: Error propagation at inter-agent message handoffs prevents MA from outperforming SA baselines. Proposes lightweight clarification module (AgentAsk) as architecture-agnostic fix.

title: On the Reliability Limits of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Planning
abstract-summary: Decision-theoretic proof that any delegated multi-agent network is dominated by a centralized Bayes decision maker with the same information. Communication introduces information loss.
notes: Formal proof that without new exogenous signals multi-agent networks are suboptimal vs centralized decision making. Communication compression causes information loss quantified via posterior divergence.

title: GUARDIAN: Safeguarding LLM Multi-Agent Collaborations with Temporal Graph Modeling
abstract-summary: Models hallucination amplification and error injection/propagation in multi-agent collaborations. Proposes temporal graph-based detection.
notes: Documents three safety failure modes: hallucination amplification across agents; agent-targeted error injection and propagation; communication-targeted error injection. Errors persist through subsequent rounds.

title: The Reasoning Trap: An Information-Theoretic Bound on Closed-System Multi-Step LLM Reasoning
abstract-summary: MAD with copies of same model produces diverse phrasings not diverse perspectives. Closed-system reasoning preserves answers while degrading evidential grounding.
notes: Formal DPI-based argument: homogeneous MAD cannot create new information. Debate preserves answer accuracy while losing evidence-grounding. Triple failure of human reliability also documented.

title: When Agents Disagree: The Selection Bottleneck in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
abstract-summary: Identifies selection bottleneck in MoA pipelines. Diversity can hurt under synthesis-based aggregation. Selection dramatically outperforms synthesis.
notes: Heterogeneous MoA teams outperform single models but homogeneous Self-MoA wins under synthesis aggregation. Closed-form crossover threshold separates where diversity helps vs hurts.

title: MedAgentBoard: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration with Conventional Methods for Diverse Medical Tasks
abstract-summary: Multi-agent does not consistently outperform single LLMs (e.g. textual medical QA) or specialized conventional methods (medical VQA; EHR prediction).
benchmark: medical QA; VQA; EHR prediction; clinical workflow
notes: Multi-agent collaboration benefits only specific scenarios (clinical workflow automation). Single LLMs and conventional methods often perform comparably or better in medical tasks.

title: Silo-Bench: A Scalable Environment for Evaluating Distributed Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract-summary: 30 algorithmic tasks; 54 configurations; 1620 experiments. Agents form coordination topologies but systematically fail to synthesize distributed state into correct answers.
notes: Communication-Reasoning Gap: agents coordinate well but fail to integrate distributed information into correct answers. Coordination overhead compounds with scale eliminating parallelization gains.

title: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent
abstract-summary: Distills multi-agent dynamics into single model weights. Motivated by high computational cost and error propagation in MA systems.
notes: Shows multi-agent debate has high computational cost and error propagation problems. Single distilled model preserves efficiency while matching multi-agent reasoning and self-correction performance.
